signals.title: USD/CAD — Geopolitical Oil Shock vs Domestic Labor Divergence
signals.text: CAD COT leveraged funds net short -82,720 contracts (21.2% long) faces conflicting weekend impulses following an oil tanker explosion via naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz alongside Friday's 68.3k Canadian employment collapse. Surging crude supply disruption risk favors CAD recovery and threatens a squeeze of extended short positioning, while the Bank of Canada pause narrative solidifies USD's +159bp SOFR-CORRA carry dominance. The Sydney market open tests whether crude risk premiums override deteriorating Canadian domestic fundamentals at Friday's 1.4254 close. Trade bias: Neutral to mildly bearish USD/CAD into the open as crude headlines prompt short-covering. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo market open response to Strait of Hormuz tanker incident. Risk: WTI fails to gap higher above $92/bbl, allowing BoC-Fed monetary policy divergence to resume USD/CAD upside toward 1.4300.

signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Middle East Supply Shock
signals.text: NOK 1W avg outperformance of +0.986% (n=2) against EUR 1W laggard contraction of -0.669% (n=9) creates an extreme 1.655% bilateral divergence reinforced by the Strait of Hormuz naval mine attack. Escalating crude supply risk amplifies Norway's terms-of-trade and real policy rate advantage (+1.82% NOK vs +0.30% EUR) while compounding economic drag across energy-dependent European importers. The Asian open acts as the catalyst for immediate cross-currency pricing of energy risk premia. Trade bias: Long NOK/EUR (short EUR/NOK) into the open. Catalyst: Energy market opening reaction to Middle East shipping disruption. Risk: De-escalation statements from regional authorities or crude failing to sustain gains above Friday's close.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short Positioning vs Fed Pricing Reversal
signals.text: EUR COT leveraged funds net short -84,775 contracts (pctl 4, z=-1.64) establishes extreme short exposure as markets slash late-October Fed hike odds down to 20%. Softening Fed policy expectations reduce USD rate support against a pair trading below all key moving averages at 1.1206, setting up short-squeeze dynamics against an oversold BEER valuation z-score of -2.27σ. Upcoming US CPI and the 28 Oct FOMC meeting will resolve the monetary policy trajectory. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/USD mean-reversion toward 1.1300 against overstretched dollar positioning. Catalyst: next Fed meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 28 Oct alongside repricing of US rate hike probabilities. Risk: US headline CPI acceleration above 0.6% reviving Fed tightening bets and breaking Friday's 1.1206 base.
